shadow:
A whole morning can pass through your hands and leave nothing behind. The hands do the dishes, the mouth answers the question, the body walks from one room to the next, and somewhere a little behind all of it the person is gone. Not asleep. Just not arrived. The morning passed and you could not say what was in it.

Most people read this as laziness or a lack of focus and try to push harder. That is the wrong door. The skating is the mind doing what minds do, which is to put everything into a line of past and next, never the thing itself, only the thought stacked beside it. It is not a defect that crept in. It is the cost of being able to think at all.

The surface shows up most in busyness. There is a kind of activity that exists only to keep the quiet from being heard, motion for the sake of not stopping. And underneath the noise the same flat feeling waits.

The way out is not louder effort. It is small and dull and slow. You begin to notice that you were absent. That noticing is already the wind getting in.
repressive: Some people meet the emptiness by switching off. The eyes go distant, the face stills, attention pulls back from the body like a tide going out. It can look like calm. It is closer to a small hiding.
reactive: Others meet the same fear by never stopping. The calendar fills, the phone stays warm in the hand, one task folds straight into the next. The motion looks like a life being lived. It is mostly a way of outrunning the silence.
gift:
The mind steps down from the chair it had been sitting in for years. The mind had been the one signing off on every choice, weighing, second-guessing, and one day it is simply not in charge anymore. The choosing still happens, lower down, in the body, in the moment it is needed.

What grows in that gap is a quiet kind of trust. Not the loud confidence built by telling yourself you are capable. This is softer and stranger. It comes from surrender, from letting life set the pace and arrive on its own terms rather than chasing it down. You start to feel, faintly, that you are held, that something is looking after the parts you cannot see.

This is also the end of a long habit of worry. Worry was the mind rehearsing futures that never came. When the rehearsing stops there is room, and a lightness moves in.

It grows in plain soil. A tidy room. Knowing where things go. Letting the small repeated acts of an ordinary day carry their own quiet instead of being rushed through on the way to some better moment. The calm you make space for keeps reaching toward something wider than calm.
siddhi:
The watcher dissolves into the watching. There is no longer a person standing back observing their life and no life being observed. There is only presence, whether the body is moving or still.

Watch a single leaf come off a tree. The leaf does not decide. The tree lets it go, and it falls completely surrendered, holding nothing. That letting go is the whole of it. And it does not happen once. Every moment the tree lets you go again, over and over, until the falling is all there is.

From here the smallest thing carries more than the grandest idea ever did. A stone. The steam off a cup before you drink. The mind quiets to a tool for speaking and nothing more, and the breath deepens, and people nearby feel it without being told, a stillness in the air around such a person.

Look back now at the surface, the skating, the long absent stretch. It was never failing. It was the in-breath before the out-breath, the dark the rest of it needed.
